entry.title: Cybersecurity Act 2: debate in Parliament
entry.summary: The Irish Council Presidency (Marian Harkin) reported progress on the three main parts of the Cybersecurity Act revision (ENISA, certification, ICT supply chains) and aims for agreement in the Council by the end of 2026, so that trilogues can start in 2027. Executive Vice-President Virkkunen put supply chain security at the core of the proposal, called for clear timelines to phase out high-risk suppliers, above all in 5G networks, and urged Parliament to give ENISA the mandate and resources it needs; she said full transposition and effective implementation of the NIS2 Directive could potentially have prevented some recent incidents or reduced their impact. Of the shadow rapporteurs, Tomas Tobé (EPP) asked for quick adoption with a framework to phase out high-risk suppliers, Jens Geier (S&D) for extending the scope to energy networks, and Markus Buchheit (ESN) opposed more resources for ENISA, a central reporting point and new certificates.
